summary: Async OCR calls block event loop + _run_async crashes from running event loop: PaddleOCRLocalAdapter.process() calls ocr_pages()/ocr_pages_with_boxes() as sync functions from async context without await/asyncio.to_thread(). Internal _run_async() double-faults (Python 3.10+ asyncio.run from running loop). All paths catch and return empty text/boxes.
failure_scenario: Submit any image/PDF for OCR through Gateway→adapter. Event loop blocked, _run_async crashes, both Gateway and legacy paths return empty results. All concurrent requests time out with 503.

summary: PDF rendering lost in adapter refactor: raw PDF bytes passed directly to ocr_pages() which expects image bytes. No PyMuPDF rendering—Image.open(pdf_bytes) fails. Multi-page PDFs collapsed to single page (index always 1). page_start/page_end range filtering removed entirely.
failure_scenario: Import any PDF through PaddleOCRLocalAdapter. PDF bytes passed to Engine.recognize() which calls Image.open() on PDF garbage—returns empty. Multi-page PDFs silently lose all but the first page's data.

summary: finished metric double-counted: both _do_recognize() (line 310) and recognize() (line 131) increment self._metrics["finished"] for the same successful request.
failure_scenario: After 500 successful remote OCR calls, metrics['finished'] reports 1000. Monitoring displays 2x throughput; capacity planning based on inflated numbers.

summary: reset_ocr_engine() became a no-op: emits DeprecationWarning + log line but does NOT reset engine state. pipeline_orchestrator.py:1187 calls it for error recovery ("Reset OCR before text fallback to avoid using corrupted model state").
failure_scenario: PaddleOCR enters corrupted state after partial failure. pipeline_orchestrator calls reset_ocr_engine() and retries—engine NOT reset, retry uses same corrupted state. All retries fail silently.

summary: Executor data key mismatch: parent sends "data_b64" but child reads "data". Every task raises KeyError and returns error. Bug documented in comments but unfixed.
failure_scenario: Using legacy subprocess executor path: every OCR page returns "error": "KeyError: 'data'". Zero OCR results. No alert because errors swallowed by broad exception handlers.

summary: Factory logs unsanitized URL: logger.info() uses config.remote_url directly instead of sanitize_url(). Credentials (user:pass@host) leak into log output.
failure_scenario: remote_url=http://admin:secret@win-paddlex:8080/ocr. Startup log exposes credentials. Visible in log aggregation system (ELK/Datadog).

summary: Executor class stripped of asyncio.Semaphore, queue capacity gate, tracking maps, and thread pool. No back-pressure on concurrent OCR. ImportError fallback removed—process pool import failure is now fatal instead of degrading gracefully.
failure_scenario: 20 simultaneous OCR requests—no semaphore gate, all pass through. Memory exhaustion or PaddleOCR thread-safety violation. If paddle not installed, ImportError propagates as 500 instead of falling back.

summary: queued metric always equals running: both incremented/decremented inside semaphore context. Should be incremented before async with self._semaphore: to measure actual queue wait time.
failure_scenario: Monitoring shows queued == running at all times. Queue buildup invisible—no way to distinguish waiting vs actively processing tasks.

summary: Unhandled httpx exception subclasses in _do_recognize: catches only ConnectError and TimeoutException. ReadError, WriteError, RemoteProtocolError propagate unhandled.
failure_scenario: PaddleX service restarts mid-request—TCP reset causes httpx.ReadError. Unhandled exception crashes calling coroutine instead of producing graceful error WorkerResult.

summary: OCR cache bypassed: new OcrEngine path never calls get_cached()/set_cached(). Every request runs full PaddleOCR inference. get_ocr_cache_stats() returns all-zero hits.
failure_scenario: Repeated OCR on identical page image (re-import preview). Each call runs full PaddleOCR—1-3 seconds per page. Cache stats show 0 hits, 0% hit rate.

summary: time.sleep() in async test handlers blocks event loop. time.sleep(0.03/0.5) serializes concurrent tasks, making concurrency tests pass artificially (serialization ≠ semaphore enforcement).
failure_scenario: test_max_concurrency_one asserts max_active[0] <= 1 but passes only because time.sleep blocks event loop—not because semaphore limits concurrency. In faster CI, test may fail or race.

summary: ocr_is_available() always returns False for PaddleX HTTP backend: checks metrics.get("alive_workers", 0) but HTTP client never produces this key.
failure_scenario: Future developer adds ocr_is_available() guard before using Gateway with execution_backend="paddlex_http". All requests fail with "OCR not available" despite healthy remote server.

summary: Too-wide except Exception in _execute_with_fallback swallows programming errors (TypeError, AttributeError) as generic fallback retry, logging at WARNING. No traceback on failure.
failure_scenario: Adapter.process() returns wrong type. TypeError caught, next backend tried. All backends fail. Developer sees "ALL_BACKENDS_FAILED" with no trace of root cause.

summary: sanitize_url strips query parameters unconditionally, including for engine fingerprint computation. Two endpoints with different query-param config produce identical fingerprints.
failure_scenario: Two PaddleX deployments: url?version=1 and url?version=2 produce identical engine fingerprints. Cannot distinguish which version processed each page in audit logs.

summary: error_type derivation inconsistent: split on "." takes last element. STABLE_ERROR_CODES mixes dot-notation and bare tokens—same error category, different casing in monitoring.
failure_scenario: Monitoring alerts on error_type: "REMOTE_CLOSED" and "remote_connect_error" are different strings. Cannot write reliable alerting rules—errors double-counted or missed.
